question.text: As of October 10, where do we keep the mobile puncture bench I call Stitch?

messages.content: I joined the Bellwether Cycle Collective's Thursday repair shift. I prefer the early shift because I cycle home before dark.
I've noted those details.
My own commuter has a belt drive. I keep its service receipts in the blue folder at home.
The collective's pump loan runs for three days. Borrowers leave their phone number on the paper loan slip.
Thanks for the update.
We charge a refundable ten-pound deposit for the floor pump. My home track pump is not part of that loan stock.
Our mobile puncture bench is the cart tagged MP-7. When I say Stitch in our workshop notes, I mean that MP-7 cart.
I've recorded that distinction.
The Stitch sewing table belongs to the upstairs costume group. I use the puncture bench for roadside demonstrations.
For my commute, the canal path is open again after the resurfacing. The east stair at the station still has no wheel ramp.
Understood.
I prefer the bridge route when carrying panniers. The repair collective's east stair is inside our building, not at the station.
The workshop's patch tins cost two pounds each. The self-adhesive patches are for demonstrations rather than our permanent repairs.
I've noted the arrangements.
I keep a rubber offcut for showing people how to roughen a surface. Our demo tyre is deliberately unrideable.
The yellow crate holds the loan helmets. Its numbered tags match the sizes on the sign-out sheet.
I've noted those details.
The helmet crate stays in the front lobby. The yellow crate on my balcony holds plant pots.
Anika Bell leads the children's balance-bike session on Saturdays. We ask parents to stay for the whole session.
Thanks for the update.
That session uses the yard behind the collective. Rain moves the balance bikes into the covered loading area.
My pannier seam needs stitching, so I booked the upstairs costume group's sewing table for September 4. They call that table Stitch too.
I've recorded that distinction.
The sewing group's fabric scissors stay upstairs. I will bring my own heavy needle for the pannier.
The autumn roadside demonstrations are at the riverside market. Tomas Adebayo brings the puncture practice tubes.
Understood.
Visitors can try fitting a patch before working on their own bike. The market organisers supply the folding chairs.
Our volunteers' first-aid refresher is September 24. The community nurse asked us to bring the yard incident book.
I've noted the arrangements.
The first-aid bag hangs by the front lobby door. The workshop spill kit stays by the parts washer.
Facilities calls cart MP-7 the roaming bench on its floor plan. That name refers to the cart, not the fixed wheel-truing bench.
I've noted those details.
The floor plan's dashed line marks the indoor evacuation route. I print the plan in large type for new volunteers.
The wheel-truing bench has a new spoke ruler. I prefer metric measurements when ordering replacement spokes.
Thanks for the update.
The fixed truing bench remains against the west wall. Its lamp has a foot switch so people can keep both hands on the wheel.
At the refresher we practised calling for help from the yard. The nurse wants the incident book checked after each shift.
I've recorded that distinction.
We agreed that children should wait with an adult during an incident. I keep the nurse's contact card with the first-aid bag.
The south porch will be enclosed for building work from October 6. Facilities offered alcove K as indoor parking for the roaming bench.
Understood.
The porch work will also close the outside tap. We will fill the cleaning bucket from the parts-room sink during that work.
Our October market session needs two tyre levers per demonstration kit. I have counted twelve sound levers.
I've noted the arrangements.
The kit bags are green so volunteers can spot them on the market table. The orange bag holds my own commuting tools.
The lobby helmet crate now has a laminated size chart. The old paper chart tore when a wet helmet was returned.
I've noted those details.
I put a drying mat under the loan helmets. Returns still go to the lobby, even while the porch work is under way.
I finished the October 6 move: the roaming bench is now in alcove K beside the collective's east stair. Its old south-porch parking spot is no longer used for it.
Thanks for the update.
The alcove's power socket is for the vacuum, not charging bike batteries. I secured the bench wheels before leaving.
The sewing group has moved its Stitch table to the upstairs cutting room. Our September pannier repair is holding up well.
I've recorded that distinction.
I will return their heavy thread spool on Friday. The cutting room is reached by the west stair.
The collective's indoor bike parking is full on Thursdays. Volunteers can lock bikes to the yard rail instead.
Understood.
I prefer the rail nearest the covered loading area. The market kit bags are packed for Saturday's demonstration.

question.text: Who was the sign-off contact for Whisk's evening beginner welcome pack on September 8?

messages.content: I'm helping Saltglass Kitchen School with its autumn welcome materials. I prefer recipes measured in grams because our scales are metric.
I've noted those details.
The school's evening beginners meet on Tuesdays. I bring my own apron rather than borrow one.
The morning bread course has a welcome sheet called Rise. Owen Tariq checks its room information.
Thanks for the update.
Rise prints on cream paper. The bread tutors want the allergy notice on the front.
Our public tasting invitations go through Celia Mensah. Those invitations cover weekend visitors rather than enrolled classes.
I've recorded that distinction.
I use plain-language directions for the tasting queue. The tasting door opens onto Market Lane.
Whisk is our working name for the E8 evening beginner welcome pack. The pack covers joining instructions for enrolled E8 students.
Understood.
The daytime beginner cohort is D3 and has a separate welcome pack called Spoon. I print both packs double-sided.
The E8 class has two portable induction rings. Students practise knife grips with carrots before using the rings.
I've noted the arrangements.
We keep spare aprons by the wash basin. Students should tie back long hair before the cooking demonstration.
I arranged a Spanish translation of the tasting invitation with Luz Ortega. Luz does translations, not course sign-off.
I've noted those details.
We reimburse her bus fare for the weekend visit. The invitation's contact number belongs to the tasting desk.
The school newsletter is called Whisk Weekly. Its editor is Dario Sanz.
Thanks for the update.
The newsletter covers every course, not just E8. I send Dario photos only after students consent.
The September evening timetable places E8 in teaching room Two. The daytime D3 class remains in teaching room One.
I've recorded that distinction.
Room Two's accessible entrance is through the courtyard. I put that route on the E8 pack's back page.
A dairy-free cake lesson has been added to the daytime Spoon course. Owen Tariq approved that course's ingredient list.
Understood.
My own preference is oat milk for tea. The staff kitchen keeps a separate jug for dairy milk.
I delivered the E8 joining packs to reception for the September 8 intake. The reception team puts them inside the enrolled students' envelopes.
I've noted the arrangements.
Tasting visitors receive a single invitation sheet. I use different envelope sizes to avoid mixing those mailings.
The school replaced a cracked chopping board in room Two. We mark the replacement with the room number underneath.
I've noted those details.
I prefer the smaller board for the onion demonstration. The old board has been taken out of teaching use.

The E8 evening beginner welcome pack had Celia Mensah as sign-off contact through September 9 inclusive. Dario Sanz took over that same sign-off role on September 10; I wrote up the completed handoff on September 14.
Thanks for the update.
Celia continues to handle public tasting invitations. The handoff concerns the enrolled E8 pack rather than those invitations.
E8 students asked for a larger map of the courtyard entrance. I will use the whole back page for the next printing.
I've recorded that distinction.
The map's dotted path avoids the kitchen loading ramp. The ramp is for deliveries, not a student entrance.
Luz returned the Spanish tasting translation with a clearer allergy sentence. Celia accepted that version for the October tasting.
Understood.
The E8 packs remain in English for this intake. Students can request a telephone explanation from reception.
The Spoon pack's course contact is still Owen Tariq. D3's next lesson is vegetable stock.
I've noted the arrangements.
I saved the stock recipe as a large-print handout. The course tutor asked for unsalted stock in the demonstration.
Dario wants the E8 welcome pack's room map checked before the October reprint. He will sign off the revised pack after that check.
I've noted those details.
The newsletter photo deadline is October 3. That deadline applies to Whisk Weekly rather than joining packs.
I sent the consented kneading photos for Whisk Weekly. One student declined, so I left that student's picture out.
Thanks for the update.
The October tasting will offer two dairy-free samples. Celia asked for separate serving spoons at those stations.
Reception now has fifty E8 welcome packs ready for the next intake. The courtyard directions were checked during yesterday's class.
I've recorded that distinction.
I stored the spare packs in the reception cupboard. The recipe handouts stay in teaching room Two.
The E8 tutor asked me to bring sticky labels for students' takeaway boxes. I prefer labels that peel off for washing.
Understood.
Our reusable boxes have blue lids. The tasting samples use paper dishes instead.

question.text: What sample rate and channel format do we currently use for Lantern Lives public listening exports?

messages.content: Lantern Lives is our neighbourhood oral-history project. I coordinate its audio preparation at Beacon Terrace Library.
I've noted those details.
Interview consent sheets are kept in the locked records cabinet. I use the interview code rather than a surname in filenames.
The project has separate folders for raw interviews and public listening exports. I put the interview date at the start of each raw filename.
Thanks for the update.
The public filenames start with the story title. Our catalogue uses the interview code to connect the two copies.
We record each interview on two memory cards. I copy both cards before erasing either one.
I've recorded that distinction.
The second card is a backup, not an extra interview. I label cards with the recorder's letter so volunteers can return them.
For Lantern Lives I remove spoken phone numbers from public listening copies. The untouched recordings remain in the restricted raw folder.
Understood.
Volunteers note redaction timecodes in the edit log. A redaction note does not change the transcript's speaker labels.
Our catalogue's 🎧 symbol means a clip needs headphones because its volume is low. I test those clips at the library's listening desk.
I've noted the arrangements.
The desk headphones are wiped after every use. I keep spare ear pads in the audio cupboard.
For Lantern Lives public listening exports, I use the profile Listening A. Archival masters use the separate profile Vault B.
I've noted those details.
The profiles are saved on the editing computer. I ask volunteers to check the export profile before starting an overnight render.
Listening A exports include a short title announcement. I leave half a second of silence before that announcement.
Thanks for the update.
We use the approved story title from the catalogue. The interviewer's name belongs in the catalogue credits, not that announcement.
The Lantern Lives transcripts use square brackets for laughter. I keep interruptions on a new line.
I've recorded that distinction.
For unclear words we use a timecode rather than guess. Volunteers can leave a comment for a second listener.
Amina Farouk reviews consent restrictions before a listening copy is published. I check technical playback after her review.
Understood.
Her review is about permission, not audio mastering. The library manager schedules the public listening sessions.
The Lantern Lives listening desk uses a playlist with one story per entry. I arrange the entries alphabetically by approved title.
I've noted the arrangements.
The desk tablet's screen timeout is ten minutes. We disable automatic playlist continuation so visitors choose their next story.
I replaced a noisy cable on recorder C. Its next test recording should include a quiet-room section.
I've noted those details.
Recorder A is booked for the September 4 interview. Volunteers collect recorders from the library equipment desk.
The Lantern Lives edit log now includes the editor's initials. I keep a separate column for consent-related cuts.
Thanks for the update.
Technical trims go in the timing column. Amina wants the consent column visible when she checks a draft.
The Lantern Lives listening room closes at five on Saturdays. Public story sessions last forty minutes.
I've recorded that distinction.
We reserve ten minutes afterward for visitor comments. Visitors can write comments anonymously on the printed cards.
For the Lantern Lives transcript index, street names use their current spelling. Historical spellings remain in the transcript when speakers use them.
Understood.
The index has a separate field for mentioned years. I do not convert approximate recollections into exact dates.
Vault B archival exports retain the original interview channel layout. I verify that both recorded channels are present before archiving.
I've noted the arrangements.
Our archive checksums are saved next to the master files. The public playlist does not contain those master files.
🎧 Export settings update: Listening A is now 48 kHz stereo after today's September 22 switch. Until September 21 it was 44.1 kHz mono.
I've noted those details.
The switch applies to new public listening exports and replacements. Vault B remains the separate archival profile.
I regenerated the Lantern Lives public playlist files with the updated Listening A profile. The desk tablet played all fourteen entries successfully.
Thanks for the update.
The playlist titles did not change. I kept the old exports in the restricted revision folder for troubleshooting.
The Lantern Lives caption sheets use eighteen-point type. Each sheet has the same title as its listening entry.
I've recorded that distinction.
We lend magnifiers at the library desk. The sheets use cream paper because several visitors found bright white uncomfortable.
Our next Lantern Lives volunteer session covers checking transcripts against audio. I will demonstrate how to record an unclear-word timecode.
Understood.
Volunteers should bring wired headphones. I booked the small meeting room so they can hear quiet passages.

question.text: Which carrier did Saltbrook Pantry finally adopt for its winter Wednesday insulated-box route as of October 9?

messages.content: I help organise deliveries for Saltbrook Pantry. Our winter Wednesday route will take insulated boxes to housebound members.
I've noted those details.
The summer Tuesday route carries dry goods. I prefer to keep separate lists for those two delivery rounds.
The pantry's front collection window is open from ten to noon. Members can nominate a neighbour to collect for them.
Thanks for the update.
We ask nominees to bring the member's collection code. I use large type on the printed collection slips.
Our insulated boxes hold six meal tubs each. The box lids have replaceable rubber seals.
I've recorded that distinction.
I wash lids separately from the tubs. The damaged seal on box Four has been removed.
Mei Anton supervises the summer Tuesday dry-goods drivers. That team uses volunteers' cars.
Understood.
The Wednesday winter delivery list is still being assembled. I do not move people between routes without checking their availability.
Plover Parcel offered to carry the winter Wednesday insulated-box route. Harbor Cart also sent a proposal for that same route.
I've noted the arrangements.
Plover quoted a per-stop price. Harbor's quote is a flat price for the round.
The pantry freezer needs a temperature check at opening and closing. I keep the check sheet on its side panel.
I've noted those details.
The freezer key hangs in the staff kitchen. Public collection volunteers use the front room rather than that kitchen.
For Wednesday insulated boxes, the food-safety volunteer recommends a maximum two-hour delivery round. We need each carrier to confirm it can meet that limit.
Thanks for the update.
The timing starts when boxes leave the pantry. Returned boxes are washed before they go back on the packing table.
The committee adopted blue tamper labels for winter meal tubs. That label decision did not choose a carrier.
I've recorded that distinction.
The labels peel off before washing. I ordered one roll to try during the packing rehearsal.
Plover Parcel said it can supply a chilled van on Wednesdays. Its proposal still needs a revised list of stops.
Understood.
The van's loading height matters for our volunteers. I asked for a photograph of its rear step.
Harbor Cart offered an assistant to lift boxes at each stop. Its quote allows twelve stops per round.
I've noted the arrangements.
We currently have eleven households on the winter list. One household needs the box left with a named neighbour.
The pantry's dry-goods stocktake is on September 30. I count opened cartons separately from sealed cartons.
I've noted those details.
We donate spare tote bags to new members. The insulated boxes remain pantry property.
Mei prefers Harbor Cart's lifting help for winter Wednesdays. Her preference is advice to the committee, not an appointment.
Thanks for the update.
I prefer Plover's chilled van if it can meet the two-hour limit. We need to compare the revised quotes before deciding.
The September 20 committee meeting deferred the winter Wednesday carrier choice. Neither proposal was accepted at that meeting.
I've recorded that distinction.
Plover still owes us its timing confirmation. Harbor was asked to price a possible thirteenth stop.
The winter packing rehearsal uses water-filled tubs rather than food. We will time how long it takes to load eleven boxes.
Understood.
I asked two volunteers to practise lifting together. The rehearsal is on the pantry premises.
Plover's photograph shows a rear step with a handrail. I forwarded it to the food-safety volunteer.
I've noted the arrangements.
Harbor has supplied the thirteenth-stop price. I kept both replies with their original proposals.
The stocktake found enough rice for the next four dry-goods rounds. We need more small tins of tomatoes.
I've noted those details.
Mei will collect the summer Tuesday mileage slips this week. Those slips do not cover the planned winter Wednesday round.
The packing rehearsal took eighteen minutes for eleven boxes. The volunteers want a trolley with larger wheels.
Thanks for the update.
The borrowed trolley belonged to the adjacent library. I returned it after the rehearsal.
The committee adopted a larger-wheeled pantry trolley for winter packing. It did not use that equipment vote to appoint a delivery carrier.
I've recorded that distinction.
Our next agenda includes the revised carrier proposals. I will bring the loading times from the rehearsal.

As of October 9, Saltbrook Pantry has not adopted a carrier for the winter Wednesday insulated-box route. Plover Parcel and Harbor Cart remain proposals; the next discussion is scheduled for October 14.
Understood.
The collection window will still open this Saturday. I am printing the current member collection codes this afternoon.
